items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: was someone I’d met before I went overseas, and he’d been corresponding with me

ctx.x: Oh that was a kind of an interesting thing because I was already aware of what was beginning to happen before the war. You see I got drafted straight off the campus, I was inducted about two or three months after I graduated from Yale. The first inkling was in the form of Dizzy Gillespie’s playing. And I first heard Dizzy in I guess it was 1938 because I remember discussing it with Marshall Stearns. His records came out and there were solos of Dizzy’s on various releases, including of course the Cab Calloway…

discharged relatively early, in fact he got discharged when his squadron was brought back to the United States from Europe in order to fly out immediately to Japan and then they were told when they were ready to go, well we don’t need you out there and those of you who have had enough service can get discharged. And that’s when he married my sister and moved out to Los Angeles, his home. But the big thing is that having had this miniature exposure as it grew, I got exposed more and more to what was happening in the New York club scene and so forth, and recording wise I wasn’t too keen on getting into it. You may be executive vice president one day,” which I never was. We got to talking about Erroll Garner.
